title: Build a competing general-purpose military data fabric / data mesh platform
problem: Services still lack one interoperable data fabric across echelons, domains and classification levels, which superficially suggests room for a new general-purpose platform; in practice the Army designated its data-layer vendors in June 2026 and the joint level standardized on Maven, so the residual pain lives in the seams, not in the absence of a platform.

user.exact_role: Program-office product owners and data architects (e.g., NGC2 data-layer product lead at CPE C2IN; CDAO enterprise data platform lead) who worry about vendor lock-in, plus the S6/G6 and knowledge-management staff who today move data between systems by hand
user.echelon: division_corps and joint (buyer); tactical_unit through theater (users of the data)
organization_examples: CDAO (Maven, Edge Data Mesh, War Data Platform)
DAF PEO C3BM (Battle Network / ABMS DI)

current_workflow: Government sets a non-prescriptive reference architecture (Army UDRA v1.0, Mar 2024; CDAO Data Mesh Reference Architecture, Mar 2024) and issues RFIs (CDAO data-mesh RFI Oct 2023; DIA Common Data Fabric RFI Dec 2024) to survey commercial capability

Program office runs competitive prototype OTAs with integrator-led teams (NGC2: Team Anduril $99.6M Jul 2025 for 4th ID; Team Lockheed $26M Sep 2025 for 25th ID) and validates in exercises (Ivy Sting/Ivy Mass, Lightning Surge)

Program office designates a baseline (Army NGC2 common data-layer baseline, Jun 22 2026: Anduril Lattice + Palantir Foundry mesh, Raft registries/transformation/federation) and moves to continuous delivery
Purchases execute as task orders under decade-long enterprise agreements (Palantir ESA up to $10B, Jul 2025; Anduril enterprise contract up to $20B, Mar 2026) rather than new competitions
Third-party capabilities onboard through the team lead's SDK (Lattice SDK, Palantir OSDK under Open DAGIR), the TAK plugin pipeline, or government-run API events (Operation Jailbreak, May 2026)
Units still bridge remaining seams manually: swivel-chair data entry, regenerating intel on coalition enclaves, thumb drives between mission networks, phone calls to negotiate cross-domain releases
current_solution: Anduril Lattice / Lattice Mesh (Army NGC2 baseline lead; CDAO Edge Data Mesh OTA $100M; Space Force SDANet), Palantir Foundry/Ontology and Maven Smart System (CJADC2 program of record, NATO MSS), Raft Data Platform (registries, transformation, federation in the Army baseline), Lockheed-integrated data layer at 25th ID, government-owned TAK Server/CoT for tactical interchange, Advana/War Data Platform at the enterprise (Accenture Federal Services integration task order up to $821M, Jul 2026), plus DDS middleware inside platforms and domain fabrics (IBCS, ABMS DI).
failure: The failure is not a missing platform. Where the fielded stack fails is at the seams: legacy systems without documented APIs (Jailbreak needed ~600 people to expose ~70 systems), the mesh stopping above tactical echelons (UDRA RFI: lower-echelon data products 'by exception only'), releasability/classification tagging that blocks sharing with allies (GAO-25-106454), enterprise ingest without interface controls or data-sharing agreements (DoD IG May 2026), immature security controls in prototypes (Army CTO memo, Oct 2025), and undefined fielding schedule and life-cycle cost (GAO-26-108019). A new general-purpose fabric would inherit every one of these seams while lacking the incumbents' designation, funding and installed base.

evidence.claim: The Army established the NGC2 common data-layer baseline on June 22 2026 with Anduril leading, partnered with Palantir (edge-to-cloud data mesh via Lattice and Foundry) and Raft (data and services registries, transformation, federation); the work falls under Anduril's 10-year enterprise agreement.
evidence.source_title: Army and industry align on common data baseline, as Next Generation Command and Control moves from prototyping to delivery
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army awarded Anduril a firm-fixed-price enterprise contract with a ceiling of up to $20B over 10 years (through March 2036) consolidating 120+ prior procurement actions; the first task order was ~$87M for JIATF-401 counter-drone C2 on Lattice. Ceiling is not obligation.
evidence.source_title: U.S. Army awards enterprise contract for IT commercial solutions
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army awarded Palantir a 10-year Enterprise Service Agreement with a maximum value of $10B consolidating 75 contracts (15 prime, 60 related); the cap is a ceiling, not a commitment.
evidence.source_title: U.S. Army Awards Enterprise Service Agreement to Enhance Military Readiness and Drive Operational Efficiency
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army's FY27 request seeks about $3.78B for NGC2 (including C2 Now / WIN-T replacement), covering integration, delivery, deployment and systems engineering of the applications, data, infrastructure and transport layers, enough to field two divisions with the full stack in FY27; the data-layer share is not broken out and the money executes through the designated teams.
evidence.source_title: Army unveils sweeping XM30 push, $4B bet on NGC2 in newly released budget materials
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO found the Army lacks a detailed fielding schedule and cost information for NGC2, raising the risk that not all units are equipped by the tentative FY2032 goal; GAO recommended CPE C2IN develop a unit-by-fiscal-year schedule.
evidence.source_title: Army Modernization: Better Schedule and Cost Information Needed to Support Scaling Battlefield Network (GAO-26-108019)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CDAO issued an RFI (responses due Nov 28 2023) on commercial data-mesh capabilities spanning multiple classification levels, fault-tolerant architectures, cloud/on-prem sync in DDIL conditions and priority-based transmission; the joint level subsequently awarded Anduril a $100M Edge Data Mesh OTA (Dec 2024) and standardized fusion on Maven rather than competing a new fabric.
evidence.source_title: Pentagon's CDAO queries industry about commercial data-mesh capabilities
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Defense Intelligence Agency posted a Common Data Fabric RFI on Dec 10 2024 with responses due Dec 20 2024; this identifies the issuing office of the sam.gov notice as DIA (IC enterprise), not a tactical C2 program office.
evidence.source_title: DIA releases common data fabric RFI
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DoD IG audit (DOWIG-2026-079, May 2026) found CDAO did not adequately verify data ingested into Advana from non-financial source systems; earlier-stage research recorded 78 of 387 source systems connected without data-sharing agreements and missing NIST interface controls; CDAO responded it should not oversee inputs/outputs.
evidence.source_title: Audit of Interface Controls Over the DoW's Advancing Analytics Repository (Report No. DOWIG-2026-079)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army's UDRA RFI states the data mesh does not yet extend to tactical echelons; lower-echelon data products are produced 'by exception only'.
evidence.source_title: Army Unified Data Reference Architecture RFI (sam.gov)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Legacy Army systems had no documented APIs; Operation Jailbreak (Fort Carson, May 2026) needed roughly 600 participants and 50+ companies to expose APIs on ~70 capabilities; 78 of ~80 vendors obtained API access.
evidence.source_title: Operation Jailbreak: the Army's massive push to hack its own systems and make them talk to each other
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO found overly restrictive classification a 'significant hindrance' to sharing C2 data with allies and across services, with no DoD entity owning the fix.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: At WFX 24-03 intelligence generated at collateral Secret could not be shared with allies; staff regenerated it on the MPE enclave with a different tool; BICES did not communicate with mission command systems.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: INDOPACOM coalition data movement relied on 'thumb drives or CDs, or sometimes people looking at two different monitors'; even after consolidation some allies cannot send attachments for lack of data-sharing policy.
evidence.source_title: INDOPACOM is replacing a pile of partner-nation networks with just one
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: An Army CTO memo reportedly flagged 'very high risk' security deficiencies in NGC2 prototypes (Oct 2025); Palantir rebutted. Current status of the deficiencies is not public.
evidence.source_title: Reuters report on Army memo on Anduril/Palantir battlefield communication system (Yahoo Finance mirror)
evidence.label: FACT (memo existence) / INFERENCE (current status)

evidence.claim: Beyond the platform owners, the layer is crowded with partial solutions: Ditto (CRDT edge sync, ATAK plugin, STRATFI up to $28M), Picogrid (Legion integration API; $9.3M AF Phase III), Tangram Flex (AFRL Phase III $95M ceiling since 2020 with no fielding evidence), XRDefense ($4.75M AF Phase III zero-trust data fabric), NT Concepts PLANK, plus government-owned TAK. Multiple SBIR-scale entrants without production evidence indicate a proto-purgatory pattern for standalone middleware.
evidence.source_title: S02 segment deep dive and E04 SBIR pattern sweep (this study), citing company and SBIR sources
evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: RECALL - not re-verified this session: Breaking Defense (Sep 2026) reported the Army readying operational NGC2 technology for I Corps beyond the 4th ID / 25th ID prototypes, i.e., the designated stack is scaling, not being recompeted.
evidence.source_title: Beyond prototypes: Army readies operational NGC2 tech for I Corps
evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because the buyer resolved the question by designation rather than by leaving a gap: the Army ran a two-team NGC2 prototype competition and then baselined Anduril/Palantir/Raft in June 2026; the joint level chose Maven as the CJADC2 cornerstone and program of record and gave Anduril the $100M Edge Data Mesh pilot; the enterprise layer went to a cost-plus integrator (Accenture Federal Services, up to $821M). Both platform owners hold decade-long enterprise agreements ($10B and $20B ceilings), so any program office that wants 'a data fabric' can order one under an existing vehicle in weeks instead of competing a new one. Government strategy (Open DAGIR, UDRA, Right to Integrate) is to own the interfaces, not to buy a second platform. Startups that tried the standalone-middleware route (Tangram Flex, Cougaar, Securboration, XRDefense) stalled at SBIR/Phase III scale; the ones that gained position (Raft, Ditto, Picogrid, Shift5, Rune) did so as components inside a team lead's stack or via a government-owned door (TAK, Tradewinds). Absence of a rival general-purpose fabric therefore reflects buyer consolidation and economics, not an unexploited opportunity.
technical_wedge: None credible for the gap as framed. A general-purpose fabric must provide schema registries, transformation, federation across clouds and edge nodes, DDIL-tolerant sync, multi-level-security tagging, an SDK ecosystem, ATO'd deployments at Secret and above, and adapters to hundreds of legacy interfaces; the incumbents have all of this funded and fielded. The only defensible technical wedges are narrow seam components that the platform owners or the government software factories would pull in: a UDRA-conformant tactical-echelon data-product catalog for DDIL nodes, an automated conformance/contract-test harness for the government-approved NGC2 API baseline, policy-aware releasability tagging and sync for coalition enclaves, or cross-fabric entity reconciliation. Those are already carried as separate gaps (G02, G05, G07, G17) and should not be confused with a platform play.

mvp.what: Not recommended as a platform. If forced: a UDRA-style data-product catalog and schema-registry service that runs on a rugged edge node, ingests CoT/TAK and open protobuf feeds, publishes data products with lineage and releasability labels, and syncs opportunistically over a simulated DDIL link.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: A three-node lab demo on commercial hardware: two disconnected 'battalion' nodes and one 'division' node exchanging synthetic CoT tracks, logistics reports and imagery metadata with conflict-free sync and per-product releasability policy, plus a conformance report against an open message standard. This demonstrates a component, not a competing fabric.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That the catalog/sync component is measurably cheaper to onboard than hand-built adapters (hours not months), survives partition and reconnection without data loss, enforces releasability labels, and can be dropped into a Lattice/TAK/Foundry-centred stack rather than replacing it.

data_requirement.what: For a platform: real sensor and program-of-record message samples, the government-approved NGC2 API baseline, Maven/Foundry ontology schemas, IBCS/ABMS interface control documents, unit data and network diagrams (CUI at minimum; Secret in exercises). For a seam component: open message standards (CoT/TAK, STANAG-style schemas, open protobuf definitions) and synthetic feeds.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Platform-level data is not obtainable outside a sponsored event (Jailbreak, Project Convergence), an SBIR with a TPOC, or a team-lead subcontract; the vendors gate SDK access to their environments. Open standards and synthetic data are freely obtainable for a component demo. A non-U.S.-person co-founder further complicates access to CUI interface documents (deemed-export review needed; not a legal conclusion).

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: They do not need to add it; they are it. Anduril and Palantir already deliver the fabric under decade-long vehicles, Raft holds the registry/federation role, and L3Harris and Northrop own the DAF and air-defense fabrics. Any adapter, catalog or sync feature a startup demonstrates can be absorbed into Lattice SDK, Foundry or Raft Data Platform within a release cycle.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: REJECT for the platform framing. The only surviving logic is a seam component sold through the incumbents' doors with an explicit expectation of licensing or acquisition by a platform owner; that is a different, narrower gap (see G02/G05/G07/G17).

capital_required.proof_of_concept_usd: $150k-$250k for a three-node open-standards component demo (two engineers, commercial edge hardware, cloud); a true platform proof of concept comparable to Lattice/Foundry is not achievable at any figure under ~$10M
capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: $2M-$5M (cleared staff, exercise participation under a team lead, CMMC/ATO groundwork, adapters to at least two programs of record) for a component; $30M-$100M+ for a platform-scale exercise demonstration
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: $10M-$25M for a component reaching a task order under a team lead vehicle; $100M+ for a platform (comparison: NGC2 prototype OTAs alone were $99.6M and $26M)
capital_required.assumptions: Figures are order-of-magnitude INFERENCE from the NGC2 OTA sizes, Picogrid's 26 SBIRs before a $9.3M Phase III, and Ditto's ~$136M raised; assumes no classified work until a facility clearance is obtained and U.S.-person control is established. LOW confidence.

regulatory_burden.explanation: Interface control documents, network diagrams and exercise data are CUI at minimum (CMMC Level 2 practices expected); NGC2 division data layers run at Secret and Maven/TITAN feeds involve SCI; production support needs cleared personnel and a facility clearance; middleware is generally EAR-controlled but adapters to weapon/C2 systems can become ITAR technical data. An ATO is required for any fielded software. These are descriptions of constraints, not legal conclusions.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder with equity or control may trigger FOCI mitigation for any facility clearance, may bar SBIR/STTR eligibility under the U.S.-ownership rule, and complicates deemed-export handling of interface data. Neither founder can currently hold a personnel clearance (U.S. citizenship required). Mitigations to review with counsel: U.S.-person control structure, keep the non-U.S. founder on unclassified/commercial or NATO-EU lines, or start in the German/NATO market. Requires a FOCI/export attorney.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Data-mesh, schema-registry and offline-first sync technology has a real commercial market (Databricks, Confluent, Ditto's commercial base), which is why Ditto can fund defense work from commercial revenue. But the commercial data-fabric market is even more crowded than the defense one, so dual use does not rescue a general-purpose military fabric; it only supports a narrow sync/catalog component.

defensibility.explanation: For the incumbents these are already proprietary: Lattice/Foundry are the designated baseline, every third-party app onboards through their SDKs, they hold ATOs at Secret, and every new integration deepens lock-in. For a new entrant nothing becomes proprietary because the government intends to own the interfaces (UDRA, Open DAGIR, Right to Integrate) and the platform owners can absorb components; the only durable asset a startup could build is a set of onboarded adapters and exercise-proven deployments inside someone else's stack.

why_now: Nothing in the last three years favors a new general-purpose fabric; the opposite happened. 2023-2024 RFIs (CDAO data mesh, DIA CDF) and reference architectures (UDRA v1.0, DMRA) surveyed the market; 2024-2025 competitive OTAs selected teams; 2025-2026 enterprise agreements ($10B, $20B) and the June 2026 baseline closed the platform question for the Army, Maven became a joint program of record, and the enterprise layer went to an integrator. What did change in the startup's favor is narrower: CRDT-based offline sync, cheap rugged edge compute, protobuf/gRPC registries and LLM-assisted schema mapping matured, and the Army's Right to Integrate / Jailbreak policy created a documented API marketplace, which favors seam components, not platforms.
killer_risk: No buyer and no path: PROBLEM (seams) -> USER (staffs) -> REQUIREMENT OWNER (CPE C2IN/CDAO) -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE all exist, but every link already terminates at Anduril/Palantir/Raft under decade-long vehicles. The Army just chose, the joint level chose Maven, the enterprise chose an integrator, and both platform owners (Anduril ~$61B valuation; Palantir ~$809M quarterly U.S. government revenue) can outspend a $250k team by four to five orders of magnitude on the same layer.

allied_extension: Marginally more open but still not a platform opportunity. NATO bought Maven Smart System NATO sole-source in six months (finalized Mar 25 2025), the UK Digital Targeting Web (GBP 1bn SDR 2025, DIP 2026 adds GBP 1.8bn) is explicitly multi-vendor, and Systematic SitaWare, Helsing and ARX hold German/NATO positions; a German co-founder gives access to Bundeswehr/NATO DIANA channels where a coalition-releasability or cross-fabric component could be sold. But a general-purpose allied fabric faces the same incumbents plus national champions, and U.S. export controls on a U.S.-built fabric would complicate allied deployment. The allied angle rehabilitates only the narrow coalition-seam version (see G17), not G28.
